advisories.title: lodash command injection via template
advisories.description: lodash before 4.17.21 is vulnerable to command injection through the template function.

advisories.title: lodash prototype pollution in defaultsDeep
advisories.description: lodash before 4.17.12 allows modification of Object.prototype via defaultsDeep.

advisories.title: minimist prototype pollution
advisories.description: minimist before 1.2.6 is vulnerable to prototype pollution via crafted arguments.

advisories.title: Express open redirect via malformed URLs
advisories.description: Express before 4.19.2 allows open redirect through improperly encoded redirect targets.

advisories.title: axios leaks the XSRF-TOKEN header to third-party hosts
advisories.description: axios before 1.6.0 sends the XSRF-TOKEN value in cross-origin requests, leaking the token.

advisories.title: node-fetch forwards cookies and authorization headers across redirects
advisories.description: node-fetch before 2.6.7 leaks sensitive headers when following a cross-site redirect.

advisories.title: serialize-javascript cross-site scripting
advisories.description: serialize-javascript before 3.1.0 allows XSS via untrusted data passed to serialize().

advisories.title: jsonwebtoken insecure default algorithm handling
advisories.description: jsonwebtoken before 9.0.0 may verify tokens with an unexpected algorithm, enabling forgery.

advisories.title: ejs template injection via prototype pollution
advisories.description: ejs before 3.1.10 lacks pollution protection, allowing server-side template injection.

advisories.title: Next.js server-side request forgery in server actions
advisories.description: Next.js before 14.1.1 allows SSRF through a crafted Host header in server actions.

advisories.title: Angular cross-site scripting in the sanitizer
advisories.description: Angular before 11.0.5 permits XSS through improperly sanitized attribute values.

advisories.title: react-dom cross-site scripting in server rendering
advisories.description: react-dom before 16.4.2 allows XSS when rendering attacker-controlled attribute names server-side.
